newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses mixed, no direction from Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses mixed, no direction from Wall St.

text.p: A shaky opening on Wall Street gave little direction to European shares which posted a mixed performance on Thursday.

On the currency front the dollar remained softer against the yen amid more signs of a burgeoning U.S. trade deficit with Japan. Mark-supportive comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer also pushed the dollar lower against the German currency.

London, Frankfurt and Paris blue chips all took heart from Wall Street's overnight surge, but French and British shares then moved into negative territory as the Dow Jones Industrial Average opened lower.
German equities bucked the trend to remain higher and London bounced back to positive ground as Wall Street nudged higher.

Uncertainty whether Wall Street could sustain a three-day rally helped to dampen morning European gains. Before its Thursday opening, the Dow Jones industrials had added back 288 points of the 700 it had lost since peaking in mid-March.

London equities remained dogged by fears that a soaring pound would hit corporate earnings later this year. Growing political uncertainties also stymied attempts to push up share prices, strategists said.
Although Britain reported slightly lower-than-expected March inflation, the positive news failed to invigorate the market.
"There are just too many unknowns at the moment so most people are just simply staying away," one senior dealer said.
Dealers said fund managers were unlikely to be aggressive buyers until after the May 1 British election, which the opposition Labour party is the odds on favourite to win, was out of the way.

German shares posted the sole strong performance among major European markets, with the IBIS electronic index trading over 0.6 percent higher. The DAX index of floor trading closed earlier 0.89 percent up on the day.

A weaker-than-expected March business sentiment report and absence of underlying inflationary concerns underpinned the market, but sentiment remained mixed and Frankfurt dealers said investors did not want to commit to large new positions.
"People are very uncertain at the moment," one dealer said.

Engineering giant Daimler Benz shed nearly 3.5 percent after analysts expressed disappointment at a meeting with management following the company results' announcement on Wednesday. Volkswagen shares received a boost as investors switched out of Daimler and into the rival carmaker.

French stocks turned negative on the back of Wall Street's decline, reversing the half a percent gains made at the open. Rumours of a government shake-up or dissolution of parliament and concerns about the country's 1997 budget deficit also put pressure on shares.
Carmaker Peugeot pulled the auto sector lower after it posted a disappointing 57 percent drop and announced a dividend cut.
In currencies, the dollar suffered against the mark to trade at 1.7250 marks after Tietmeyer said that the Bundesbank had no interest in further weakening of the German currency.
A sharp rise in Japan's March overall trade surplus with the United States weakened the dollar against the yen as fears of heightening trade tension between the two countries grew.
The United States reported a surprise jump in February imports, boosting the country's overall trade deficit above Wall Street expectations.
U.S. officials have issued a stern warning of trade friction unless Japan became less reliant on exports and promoted growth from within.
Japanese authorities appear eager to let some steam out of the dollar's rally but would be happy to see a gentle landing that keeps the U.S. currency on a firm trend against the yen, analysts said.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7250 marks and 125.83 yen after ending at 1.7285 and 125.80 in late trading in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 2.0 points at 4,292.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 10.95 points lower at 2,610.02.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS electronic index was 21.76 points higher at 3,369.30. The 30-share DAX index closed up 29.80 points at 3,383.25.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $340.40 in London versus $339.65 at the close in London on Wednesday. Silver was eight cents lower at $4.72.
